name: New Horizons
tagline: First spacecraft to fly past Pluto, then on to the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth
description: New Horizons is NASA's spacecraft to Pluto and the Kuiper Belt, the first mission of the New Frontiers program. The Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory built it, and Alan Stern of Southwest Research Institute is its principal investigator. It launched on an Atlas V 551 from Cape Canaveral on 2006-01-19 with a mass of 478 kg, and it carries seven instruments and a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) that was a spare from Cassini. After a gravity assist at Jupiter on 2007-02-28, it flew past Pluto on 2015-07-14 at 12,500 km, the first spacecraft to explore the dwarf planet up close, and past the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth on 2019-01-01 at about 3,500 km. It is still operating in its Kuiper Belt Extended Mission, observing distant Kuiper Belt objects.
best_known_for: First spacecraft to explore Pluto up close, then flew past Arrokoth in 2019, the most distant object ever explored up close
